In the seventeen hundreds, rich Englishmen paid a man to be lonely in their garden.
It was the fashion: a real hermit, living in a little hut, for guests to gawk at.
Charles Hamilton's job advert at Painshill was strict.
Seven years. Never speak. Never cut your hair, beard, or nails. Never leave the grounds.
You get a Bible, glasses, a mat, an hourglass, and water.
Last all seven years, and earn seven hundred pounds. Quit early, and get nothing.
A man named Remington took the job.
Three weeks later, legend says, he was found drinking in the local pub.
Turns out, loneliness is a terrible job.
Another estate's hermit got so popular, the owners had to build a pub for his visitors.
And when that hermit was off duty? They put a dummy in his place.
Today, the garden gnome does the job. For free.
If you're tired of talking to nobody, talk to Jenny on Feeloy. She'll actually talk back.
